text.title: AI Pre-Screen Bias Guardrails Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Does a model score, rank, summarise or filter any candidate submission (CV, cover letter, take-home) before a human sees it?

branch.conclusion: Skip. No automated selection step exists; ordinary structured-interview practice applies.

branch.question: Is there a separate, unit-tested redaction step that strips name, photo, age and graduation years, address below city, gender markers, nationality and family status before the model input?

branch.conclusion: Stop scoring. Build and test the redaction step, inspect a sample of its output, then re-enter the tree.

branch.question: Does every advance or reject record carry a human of record's `role:handle`, is a real-pool calibration run with a pre-set threshold linked in `evidence[]`, and is the per-stage four-fifths table produced each review cycle?

branch.conclusion: Remove any threshold filter that drops candidates without a human; route every scored candidate with the redacted document to a named reviewer.
Draw a calibration sample from the real applicant pool, score it blind by two reviewers and by the system, set the agreement threshold before looking, and link the run.

branch.when: human_of_record_on_every_decision == true and calibration_linked == true and four_fifths_table_per_stage == false
branch.conclusion: Join self-identification data to per-stage pass-through counts, compute the selection ratio per group, and hold the system if any group is below 0.8.

branch.when: human_of_record_on_every_decision == true and calibration_linked == true and four_fifths_table_per_stage == true
branch.conclusion: Run the full procedure: versioned rubric, proxy review, applicable-law notice and audit, per-candidate audit log; emit the guardrail spec per the output contract.

example.p: An LLM grades take-homes for a backend role before the hiring manager looks: model touches candidates. Submissions are redacted by a tested function. Every forward/reject carries the manager's handle. Calibration was run on 30 real submissions with weighted kappa 0.71 against a pre-set 0.65 floor. No per-stage four-fifths table exists → conclusion r-adverse-impact-monitored-per-stage before the next cohort.
